stemMd: Two cyclists move in the same direction at constant speeds 9 m/s and 6 m/s. How quickly does the faster cyclist gain on the slower one?
explanationMd: For motion in the same direction, relative speed is the difference, 9−6=3 m/s. The faster cyclist gains three metres each second.

distractorRationale.a: This divides speeds rather than subtracting.
distractorRationale.c: This uses the slower cyclist's speed alone.
distractorRationale.d: This is the closing speed for opposite directions.
